- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is falling, model underestimates drop; add 1–3% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to recent sentiment swings; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment > 0.6, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day; if < 0.4, increase by 1–2%.
- When true outcome is below 70, model frequently misses the bottom; add 5–10% downward bias if sentiment is weak and price has been trending down for 3+ days.
- Avoid forecasting based on 30-day history alone; if sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), use 14-day rolling average for smoother correction.
